source: Starting data from the Boise State sheets 'Fall 2026 - CE 323 Inventory - Updated 7_28_26', the 2022 and 2023 inventories, 'CE323 Resupply List' and 'Alkalinity and Acidity Lab Supplies'. Per-section amounts are the sheet's semester totals (3 tests per lab x 4 lab sections) divided by 4. Counts are as of 2026-07-28; do a fresh count before relying on them.

labs.name: Alkalinity
labs.about: Titrate a water sample with acid to find how much it resists a drop in pH. Two endpoints: pH 8.3 (phenolphthalein) and pH 4.5 (total alkalinity).

labs.name: Acidity
labs.about: Titrate a water sample with sodium hydroxide to find how much base it takes to neutralize it.

labs.name: Hardness
labs.about: Titrate with EDTA to measure calcium and magnesium (total hardness), then calcium alone.

labs.name: Molecular parameters
labs.about: Hach colorimetric and titration tests for ammonia, chloride, fluoride, iron, manganese, orthophosphate and sulfate.

labs.name: Jar test
labs.about: Add different doses of alum to jars of turbid water, mix, let settle, and find the best coagulant dose.

labs.name: Settling column
labs.about: Watch particles settle in a tall column and sample at depths and times to build isoremoval curves.

labs.name: Filtration
labs.about: Run coagulated water through a filter column and sample turbidity over time.

labs.name: Turbidity sampling
labs.about: Measure turbidity of samples with the turbidimeter.

labs.name: BOD and dissolved oxygen
labs.about: Measure dissolved oxygen by the Winkler (azide) titration and set up 5-day BOD bottles.

labs.name: Suspended solids
labs.about: Filter a sample through a weighed glass fiber filter, dry it and weigh it again.

items.name: Sulfuric acid, 0.2 N (titrant)
items.about: The acid you add from the burette in the alkalinity titration. The volume used tells you the alkalinity. You can also make it from the 1.0 N stock.

items.name: Sulfuric acid, 1.0 N stock (1 L)
items.about: Stock solution. 200 mL diluted to 1 L with DI water makes 0.2 N titrant. Only dilute with Dr. Miller's OK and proper PPE.

items.name: Sodium hydroxide, 0.2 N (titrant)
items.vendor: Made in lab (from the 5.0 N stock)
items.about: The base you add from the burette in the acidity titration. Made from the 5.0 N stock.

items.name: Sodium hydroxide, 5.0 N stock (1 L)
items.about: Stock solution. 40 mL diluted to 1 L with DI water makes 0.2 N titrant. Only dilute with Dr. Miller's OK and proper PPE.

items.name: Phenolphthalein indicator solution (100 mL dropper)
items.about: Pink above pH 8.3, colorless below. Marks the first alkalinity endpoint and the acidity endpoint. About 12 drops per section.

items.name: Methyl orange indicator solution (100 mL dropper)
items.about: Changes from yellow to orange-red near pH 4.5, the total alkalinity endpoint. About 12 drops per section.

items.name: Bromcresol green-methyl red indicator powder pillows
items.about: One pillow per titration. Indicator for the total alkalinity endpoint (pH 4.5) with the Hach digital titrator.

items.name: Phenolphthalein indicator powder pillows
items.about: One pillow per titration. Same job as the phenolphthalein solution, for the Hach digital titrator method.

items.name: Bromphenol blue indicator powder pillows
items.about: One pillow per titration. Indicator for the acidity endpoint with the Hach digital titrator.

items.name: Sulfuric acid digital titrator cartridge, 0.1600 N
items.about: Clicks into the Hach digital titrator. Turning the knob delivers acid in counted 'digits'. About 900 digits are used per semester, so one opened cartridge usually lasts.

items.name: Sodium hydroxide digital titrator cartridge, 0.1600 N
items.about: Digital titrator cartridge for acidity. About 250 digits are used per semester.

items.name: Digital titrator delivery tubes
items.about: The clear J-shaped tube that goes on the end of a titrator cartridge. One per titrator; swap when cloudy or cracked.

items.name: Hardness 1 buffer solution
items.about: Holds the sample at pH 10 so the EDTA titration for total hardness works. About 3 mL per section.
items.notes: Fisher sells a 100 mL bottle for $42.37.

items.name: Eriochrome Black T indicator
items.about: Wine-red when calcium and magnesium are present; turns blue at the EDTA endpoint.

items.name: EDTA standard titrant, 0.01 M
items.about: The titrant for hardness. EDTA grabs calcium and magnesium; the volume used tells you the hardness. About 12.5 mL per section.

items.name: CalVer 2 calcium indicator powder pillows
items.about: Indicator for calcium hardness only (used after raising the pH with 8 N potassium hydroxide).

items.name: Potassium hydroxide, 8 N
items.about: Raises the pH to about 12 so magnesium drops out and only calcium is titrated. Very caustic. About 3 mL per section.

items.name: ManVer 2 hardness indicator powder pillows
items.about: Indicator for total hardness with the Hach digital titrator.

items.name: Sulfuric acid standard solution, 5.25 N (100 mL dropper)
items.about: Listed in the hardness module (about 4.5 mL per section). Strong acid; see the lab procedure for its step.

items.name: EDTA digital titrator cartridge, 0.0800 M
items.about: Digital titrator cartridge for low-hardness samples. About 700 digits per semester.

items.name: EDTA digital titrator cartridge, 0.800 M
items.about: Digital titrator cartridge for high-hardness samples. About 700 digits per semester.

items.name: Ammonia salicylate reagent powder pillows (10 mL)
items.about: Ammonia test, first pillow. Always used together with the cyanurate pillow.

items.name: Ammonia cyanurate reagent powder pillows (10 mL)
items.about: Ammonia test, second pillow. Develops the green color you read on the spectrophotometer.

items.name: Diphenylcarbazone indicator powder pillows (chloride)
items.about: Indicator for the chloride titration with mercuric nitrate.
items.notes: The 2026 sheet asks whether Chloride 2 indicator works instead.

items.name: Mercuric nitrate digital titrator cartridge, 0.2256 N
items.hazard: Contains mercury. Collect all chloride waste in the labeled waste container.
items.about: Titrant for chloride. About 70 digits per semester.

items.name: SPADNS fluoride reagent solution (1 L)
items.hazard: Read the safety data sheet before use and dispose of waste as directed.
items.about: Fluoride reagent read on the spectrophotometer. About 12 mL per section.

items.name: FerroVer iron reagent powder pillows (10 mL)
items.about: Iron test. Turns the sample orange in proportion to the iron in it.

items.name: Alkaline cyanide reagent (manganese, 50 mL dropper)
items.hazard: Contains cyanide. Never mix with acid. Dispose of as directed.
items.about: Manganese (PAN method) reagent. About 36 drops per section.

items.name: Ascorbic acid powder pillows (manganese)
items.about: First step of the manganese (PAN) test.

items.name: PAN indicator solution, 0.1% (manganese)
items.about: Manganese test indicator; develops the orange color you read. About 36 drops per section.

items.name: PhosVer 3 phosphate reagent powder pillows
items.about: Orthophosphate test. Turns the sample blue in proportion to phosphate.
items.notes: Check the pillow size (10 mL or 25 mL) matches the procedure. USABlueBook stocks the 25 mL pillows (212599).

items.name: SulfaVer 4 sulfate reagent powder pillows
items.about: Sulfate test. Makes the sample cloudy in proportion to sulfate.

items.name: Sample cells, 1-inch square glass, 10 mL
items.about: The glass vials that go into the DR3900 spectrophotometer. Keep them clean and scratch-free.

items.name: Aluminum sulfate (alum), ACS grade
items.about: The coagulant. It makes tiny clay particles clump into flocs that settle. Used in all of Module 2.

items.name: Bentonite clay
items.about: Mixed into tap water to make the turbid 'raw water' for Module 2.

items.name: Silicone oil (small dropper bottle)
items.about: About 2 drops per test tube in Module 2; roughly one bottle a year.
items.notes: The 2026 sheet wasn't sure which kind; the Fisher number is from the 2023 order.

items.name: BOD nutrient buffer pillows, 6 L
items.about: One pillow feeds 6 L of BOD dilution water with nutrients so the microbes can grow.

items.name: BOD nutrient buffer pillows, 19 L
items.about: Same as the 6 L pillow, for a 19 L carboy of dilution water.

items.name: Alkaline iodide-azide reagent powder pillows
items.hazard: Contains sodium azide. Do not mix with acid.
items.about: Winkler dissolved oxygen test, step 2 (after manganous sulfate). About 12 per section.

items.name: Manganous sulfate powder pillows
items.about: Winkler dissolved oxygen test, step 1. About 12 per section.

items.name: Sulfamic acid powder pillows
items.about: Winkler dissolved oxygen test, step 3. Dissolves the floc and frees iodine for titration. About 12 per section.

items.name: Sodium thiosulfate standard solution (1 L)
items.about: Titrant for the Winkler dissolved oxygen test.

items.name: Starch indicator solution (500 mL)
items.about: Turns blue-black with iodine. When the blue disappears during the thiosulfate titration, you've hit the endpoint.

items.name: Glass fiber filters, 47 mm (Whatman 934-AH)
items.about: Catches the suspended solids. Each filter is weighed, used once, dried and weighed again. About 5 per section.

items.name: Aluminum weighing dishes, 42 mm
items.about: Hold each filter while it dries in the oven. 42 mm was the size chosen in Nov 2025.

items.name: Nitrile gloves, extra large
items.notes: The July 2026 count was one opened box.

items.name: Kimwipes
items.about: Lint-free wipes for cleaning sample cells and probes.

items.name: Graduated cylinders, 250 mL
items.about: One per group.

equipment.name: pH meter stands (Fisher Accumet AE150)
equipment.notes: All power cords accounted for; all units turn on.

equipment.name: pH probes (Fisher 13-620-AE6)
